literal: Sky-high appearance what will it do, if one's own mind falls into guilt known to oneself?
translation: Of what use is an imposing, sky-high appearance of holiness if one's own mind is conscious of a sin committed?
modern: தன் நெஞ்சம் அறிய ஒருவன் தவறு செய்வானானால், அவனுடைய வானளவு உயர்ந்த தவக்கோலம் அவனுக்கு என்ன நன்மையைச் செய்யும்?
explanation: This couplet exposes the emptiness of external religious or ascetic posturing when unaccompanied by inner purity. The poet asks what benefit a 'sky-high appearance' (வானுயர் தோற்றம்)—referring to the grand outward garb or posture of an ascetic—can possibly bring if the person's own conscience (தன்னெஞ்சம்) is fully aware of a hidden sin (தான்அறி குற்றம்) they have committed. True virtue is defined by the purity of the mind, and outward displays cannot mask or cure a guilty conscience.
